newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap -Gas oil hangs on to early gains.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap -Gas oil hangs on to early gains.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady late afernoon on Wednesday following a big increase in the morning on the back of a hefty 57-cent gain to overnight crude, traders said.
"Gas oil is up on crude and some East-West play, but there is not much strength fundamentally," one trader said.
August swaps were indicated at $21.60/$21.70 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $21.20/$21.30.
August traded in the morning at $21.70 and $21.75 before easing slightly to trade at $21.65, brokers said. It traded in the afternoon at $21.60.
The August/September contango came off slightly but still traded at a wide range of minus 80 cents earlier in the day, down from Tuesday's trade of minus 85 cents, brokers said.
The firmer prices was largely put down to the 57-cent jump to overnight August Brent crude futures which closed at $18.41 per barrel.
Brent last traded lower in London at $18.35 per barrel, down four cents.
Traders said swaps was also held up by trading firms and banks who were playing the East-West spread by buying the East and selling the West.

The physical gas oil market remained weak due to ample surplus prompt cargoes amid poor regional demand, with China still sorely missing from the market, while the recent flow to South America was said to have ended.
Traders said physical sellers were expected to maintain their aggressive offers in an effort to get rid of prompt barrels.
On Tuesday, cargoes were offered down to a low of $20.50 per barrel but no buyers emerged.
Fuel oil swaps were steady with August and September last quoted unchanged at $98.00/$99.00.
September traded earlier in the day at $98.75.
Naphtha swaps rose sharply along with the stronger crude and a prompt physical squeeze.
August was last quoted at $21.65/$21.80 per barrel, up from Tuesday's $21.30 traded level.
